oneLiner: Exact, product-aware pool and hot tub chemistry calculators: how much of *your* chemical to add to *your* water, with the reasoning shown and a simple test log.
audience: Residential pool owners doing their own maintenance, chlorine and saltwater pools (US first: gallons, ounces, pounds; also litres, grams and kilograms)
Hot tub and spa owners (small volumes, where dosing errors matter more)
New owners who don't yet know what FC, CC, TA, CYA or LSI mean
mustHave: LSI/CSI calculator using the standard formula (pH, temperature, calcium hardness, total alkalinity with a CYA correction, TDS)
Recommended ranges page with a cited source per range (e.g
competitors: Search for these by name: swimuniversity (calculator inside a content site), poolchemcalculators, waterbalancetools, poolchemtracker, poolchemicalcalculator, simplifiedpools, poolformula. Trouble Free Pool's Pool Math app is the trusted name among enthusiasts. Most web calculators handle one chemical form, ignore side effects, or don't show their working. Beat them with product-specific dosing, side effects and cited ranges.
monetization: The owner may add affiliate links (test kits, chemicals) or ads later. Never add them yourself.
doneText:
# DONE: ClearPoolMath v1 to v5

Canonical host: `https://clearpoolmath.netlify.app`. The sitemap lists 42 pages plus the home page's links. Pages from v1 and v2 are in `.ai/done-v2.md`, v3 in `.ai/done-v3.md`, v4 in `.ai/done-v4.md`. v5 added:

| Page | Target keyword |
|---|---|
| `/breakpoint-chlorination-calculator/` | breakpoint chlorination / combined chlorine (lib `breakpoint.js`) |
| `/salt-chlorinator-output-calculator/` | salt cell output setting (lib `swg.js`) |
| `/what-to-add-to-my-pool/` | what to add to my pool from test results (lib `today.js`) |
| `/liquid-chlorine-vs-tablets/` | liquid chlorine vs tablets (lib `compare.js`, data `chlorine-ph.json`) |
| `/pool-cover-savings-calculator/` | solar / pool cover savings (lib `coversave.js`, data `cover-savings.json`) |
| `/can-you-mix-pool-chemicals/` | can you mix pool chemicals (text page, CDC and EPA sources) |
| `/pool-leak-bucket-test-calculator/` | pool leak bucket test (lib `leak.js`) |

Also: the volume calculator now has an "Oval with straight sides" shape (stadium formula), so the 8 to 12% ellipse under-read has a proper alternative.

## Test results
`npm test` green at last push: 193 unit tests, 350 browser tests, check OK.

## Skipped (and why)
- Borate calculator: no primary per-ppm dosing source found, only product labels.
- Salt cell chart by model and bromine dose: manufacturer sources unreachable or contradictory (carried from v4).

## Unsure / worth a human look
- The leak test treats a difference over 1/16 inch as a leak, and needs 6+ hours. That threshold is this site's own judgment (stated on the page), not a published standard.
- The mixing page's facts (never mix chlorine with acid or different chlorine products; storage below 95 °F) are from the CDC pool chemical safety page and EPA-registered labels via search; WebFetch is blocked so the pages were not read in full. A human should read it once.
- The volume calculator's straight-sided oval unit test uses the textbook stadium area (MathWorld) and matches the chart page, but has no manufacturer's gallon figure behind it.
- Most data entries are `"via": "search"`.
- History note: `origin/main` was force-updated by something outside this loop at the start of run 6. The older local line was kept as the local branch `backup-old-main` (not pushed).

## Owner launch checklist
1. Check Netlify serves `https://clearpoolmath.netlify.app/`.
2. Add it to Google Search Console as a URL-prefix property and submit `/sitemap.xml`.
3. Buy clearpoolmath.com when there is budget, then tell the loop to switch the canonical host.

## 10 best next pages
1. Pool pump size / flow rate calculator (turnover and head loss, needs a verified source).
2. Pool water balance for hot weather: chlorine loss vs sun and temperature, if a cited source appears.
3. Salt cell chart and bromine dose, once manufacturer sources are reachable.
4. Borate calculator, if a primary dosing source is found.
5. Pool heat-up time calculator (BTU, volume, rise in °F; extends the heater page).
6. Saltwater pool vs chlorine pool running cost comparison (reuses `runcost.js`).
7. Pool shock schedule: how often to shock by season and use (cited).
8. Cloudy pool water causes and fix, a diagnostic page linking each dose tool.
9. Hot tub chemical calculator by dose (bromine and chlorine), if sources agree.
10. Above ground pool liner size calculator (liner types and overlaps, needs maker sources).
